To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we established the reference intervals of the most important clinicopathological parameters for two groups of piglets, and that we observed that the values of these parameters are significantly different between these two groups.

1) piglets have a high variability in haematology and biochemistry compared to adults; 2) piglets have higher RBC, HCT, and Hb and lower MCV compared to adults; and 3) piglets are iron deficient, even when parenteral iron is administered.
the reference intervals for haematochemistry in piglets are age-dependent and the iron supplementation is necessary in the first days of life to avoid iron deficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the welfare and the health of the animals, as well as with the reduction of the number of animals used.
the development of a new-born piglet model, which can represent an alternative to adult pigs in biomedical research.
the establishment of new reference intervals for haematochemical parameters in young pigs, which are essential for a better understanding of the physiological and pathological changes in piglets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reference intervals of the piglet are different from those of the adult pig and are also different according to age.

this study provides valuable reference intervals for piglets at two specific ages and can be used in the near future as a historical control improving the reduction in animal experiments as suggested by the Reduction, Refinement and Replacement (3Rs) principle.

the present work provides valuable reference data that can be used in the preclinical field to establish the normal range of haematological and biochemical parameters in two different age groups of piglets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
piglets are not miniature adult pigs, and they must be considered as different species.
the piglet represents a valuable animal model in the preclinical research field, but it should be considered that the piglet physiology differs from that of the adult pig.
piglets are a useful animal model for human studies, but the results should be interpreted carefully.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age of the animal should be taken into account when interpreting clinicopathological data.
piglets should not be treated as miniature versions of adult animals.
piglets have different reference intervals from adult pigs and, for this reason, it is not possible to use adult laboratory reference values for piglets.
